newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine, Russia fail to agree gas transit tariffs.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine, Russia fail to agree gas transit tariffs.

text.p: Ukraine's oil and gas body and Russia's RAO Gazprom failed to agree transit tariffs for Russian gas crossing Ukrainian territory to Europe this week, a top official said on Wednesday.

"The talks ended with nothing. We will negotiate further. Russia wants to pay $1.75 per 1,000 cubic metres, we want a higher price," said Olexander Sverdlov, head of the transit department of Ukraine's State Oil and Gas Committee.
"We would like to charge European prices for transit -- some of them are twice the Russian proposal," he told Reuters.
Ukrainian negotiators met Gazprom chief Rem Vyakhirev for talks in Moscow on Monday and Tuesday.
Up to now Russia has paid a nominal price for gas crossing Ukraine, which owes Gazprom about $1.6 billion for gas supplied between 1993 and 1995.
Last month Vyakhirev met Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma in Kiev. They agreed that a 20-year gas supply deal should be drawn up.
Ukraine hopes such an agreement would end uncertainty over the terms of gas supplies to Ukraine, which is dependent on Russia for much of its energy needs.
The deal also aims to fix transit charges for Russian gas supplies to Europe through Ukrainian territory until 2020.
Russia sends up to 120 billion cubic metres of gas a year to European customers via Ukraine and about 50 billion cubic metres to Ukraine itself.
Sverdlov denied construction of an alternative $40 billion Yamal-Europe gas pipeline through neighbouring Belarus, launched last month, had strengthened Russia's positions at the talks.
"There was no blackmail from Russia. It's clear it would take years and years to complete the project," Sverdlov said.
Experts say that with the alternative gas pipeline Russian supplies to Europe via Ukraine would drop by almost half.
The row over gas mirrors another one which has marred bilateral relations since the collapse of the former Soviet Union -- on oil transit charges across Ukraine.
Kiev increased prices for Russian oil crossing to Europe through the Druzhba (Friendship) pipeline to $5.20 per tonne on January 1, from a previous $4.75.
